Package com.bilt.pos.session

Class SettlementFlow

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.session.SettlementFlow
public final class SettlementFlow extends Object
The settlement orchestration chain returned by TerminalShopperSession.settle().

Registering handlers sends nothing. With the default settlement option, the sequence is refund allocations (including external register-managed refunds), rebate redemption, point redemption, stored value line fulfillment, stored value tender, card charge, and award. With net settlement, only the signed basket difference is charged or refunded. The sequence runs when execute() (asynchronously, on the session's operation thread), executeSync() (blocking), get(), or getOrNull() is invoked. Each step handler receives that step's result and returns the updated total for the next step (letting the register recompute tax on discounted amounts). 


 session.settle()
     .onRebatesRedeemed(rebates -> rebates.getSuggestedTotal())
     .onPointsRedeemed(points -> points.getSuggestedTotal())
     .onSuccess(result -> register.printReceipt(result.getMerchantReceipt()))
     .onError(error -> SettlementRecovery.abort())
     .execute();

With execute(), every handler — the step handlers, onSuccess, onError, and onComplete — is delivered through the callback executor (the session builder's callbackExecutor, or the per-flow callbackOn(Executor) override), and the settlement thread waits for each answer: the handlers are part of the settlement negotiation, so their return values steer the sequence exactly as if they ran inline — they just physically run on the integrator's thread. Keep them quick (settlement is paused while they run), and never block a callback thread on this flow's get() — the flow would be waiting on that thread's handler while it waits on the flow. Without a callback executor, handlers run directly on the thread executing the sequence.

If a charge-side terminal request has an indeterminate outcome, the SDK first resolves it through TransactionStatus. A recovered success continues without calling onError; a recovered failure or authoritative not-found result is reported as definitive. onError also receives an indeterminate failure when TransactionStatus itself cannot resolve the request. Its SettlementRecovery retries only the failed step, skips an optional step, records an external final tender, aborts and unwinds, or abandons the partial flow to the register. Earlier successful steps remain committed unless the register returns SettlementRecovery.abort(). Refund allocation failures are different: they are not retried in the same run, and committed refund allocations are not unwound. Retry by calling settle() again with the same committed allocation prefix. The default charge-side policy (no handler) is abort().

Movement callbacks are immediate observations, not the authoritative final ledger. An abort may reverse charge-side movements, and retrying, skipping, or replacing a partially committed failed step first reverses only that step's partial movements. Each movement the SDK reverses successfully is reported again through onMovement(java.util.function.Consumer<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementMovement>) as a reversal notice (SettlementMovement.isReversal()), and a card payment also through onCardChargeReversed(java.util.function.Consumer<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementMovement>); a movement whose reversal failed stays standing, with no notice. Refund allocation movements are durable because settlement never unwinds them. Treat SettlementResult.getMovements() from a successful result as the final movement ledger.

  • Field Details

    • MAX_AUTOMATIC_CARD_REQUESTS

      public static final int MAX_AUTOMATIC_CARD_REQUESTS
      How many card requests a settlement without onPartialCardApproval(java.util.function.Function<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.PartialCardApproval, com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.PartialApprovalDecision>) sends for a shortfall: the request that came back partial counts as the first, so the SDK adds at most MAX_AUTOMATIC_CARD_REQUESTS - 1 automatic follow-up requests per settlement. Planned card payments (SettlementOptions.cardPayments) and requests the register retries do not count. A Bilt rewards payment the terminal answered as partial (its points leg, with no card in it) is a request to the terminal and counts like a card request: after it, at most two card requests follow. When the last request allowed comes back partial too, that card step fails as DECLINED to onError(java.util.function.Function<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementFailure, com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementRecovery>), with the earlier card payments still committed: abort() (the default) reverses them all, and retry() or external() first reverse that last partial charge.
      See Also:

    • callbackOn

      public SettlementFlow callbackOn(Executor executor)
      Delivers this flow's handlers through executor instead of the session's default callback executor. Affects execute() only — the synchronous paths always dispatch on the calling thread.

    • beforeStep

      public SettlementFlow beforeStep(Function<SettlementContext,String> handler)
      Called before each step; returns the SaleTransactionID to use for that step. Default: the basket's shared sale transaction ID, carried by every checkout request of that basket.

      A split settlement (SettlementOptions.cardPayments) calls it before every card payment. Card payments after the first must reuse the first card payment's ID, as nexo requires of split payments: for them the context's default ID is that ID, and returning any other ID fails that card payment before anything is sent, as a throwing handler does: onError(java.util.function.Function<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementFailure, com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementRecovery>) gets an INVALID_STATE failure with the amount still due and the card payments already committed, and decides as for any card payment failure.

    • onCardCharged

      public SettlementFlow onCardCharged(Consumer<SettlementMovement> handler)
      Called when a card charge leg commits: once per card payment, so several times for a split settlement (SettlementOptions.cardPayments). See onMovement(java.util.function.Consumer<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementMovement>) for the provisional charge-side callback contract.

      It also fires for a payment request the terminal paid partly or entirely with Bilt rewards (implicit loyalty): the movement's SettlementMovement.getBiltRewardsAmount() is the rewards part, and equals SettlementMovement.getAmount() when no card was in it — a Bilt rewards payment, which the result reports in SettlementResult.getBiltRewardsPayments() rather than as a card payment. It is null for a card-only payment.

    • onCardChargeReversed

      public SettlementFlow onCardChargeReversed(Consumer<SettlementMovement> handler)
      Called when the settlement itself successfully reverses a card payment it had already reported through onCardCharged(java.util.function.Consumer<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementMovement>): before retry() or external() replaces a failed card step whose charge had committed (a partial approval the SDK could not keep, a handler that threw after the charge, a TransactionStatus-recovered charge whose processing failed), and for each card payment an abort() unwind reverses. The movement is a reversal notice (SettlementMovement.isReversal()): SettlementMovement.getReversedMovement() is the card payment, and its ServiceID and POI reference are the reversal's. A charge whose reversal failed gets no notice: it stays standing for voidTransaction(), as before. onMovement(java.util.function.Consumer<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementMovement>) receives every reversal notice too, those of the other charge-side steps included, and each of the two gets the notice even when the other throws. A handler that throws is logged and the reversal goes on. Reversals that run outside a settlement (a retried settle() finishing the standing movements an earlier unwind left, or voidTransaction()) report through their own results, not through this callback.

      Like onCardCharged(java.util.function.Consumer<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementMovement>), it also fires for a reversed payment Bilt rewards paid part or all of: the notice's SettlementMovement.getBiltRewardsAmount() (and its reversed movement's) is the rewards part, and equals the amount for a Bilt rewards payment.

    • onPartialCardApproval

      public SettlementFlow onPartialCardApproval(Function<PartialCardApproval,PartialApprovalDecision> handler)
      Called when a card payment commits with less than it requested: the terminal answered Partial with an AuthorizedAmount below the RequestedAmount. The payment's movement and onCardCharged(java.util.function.Consumer<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementMovement>) fire first. The returned PartialApprovalDecision charges the shortfall on another card, adds it to the next card payment, records a register-managed payment for everything still due, or aborts and reverses every card payment. Card brand rules require an unpaid partial approval to be reversed, so a sale the shopper cannot finish must abort.

      Without this handler, the SDK keeps a partial approval and sends another card request for the shortfall, as PartialApprovalDecision.anotherCard() does, up to MAX_AUTOMATIC_CARD_REQUESTS. A registered handler replaces that default entirely and has no limit: it can count PartialCardApproval.getCardPayments() itself.

      With implicit loyalty and multi-tender on the terminal, the partial payment can be the terminal's Bilt rewards leg: rewards paid part of the sale and no card was in it. The handler is called for it like for a card (PartialCardApproval.isBiltRewards() tells them apart), and the default sends a card request for the rest.

      The handler is never called for a sale with cashback (a partial there, including a refused cashback, fails as DECLINED, with or without the handler), nor for an authorization of zero, which is a decline. A handler that throws or returns null is reported to onError(java.util.function.Function<com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementFailure, com.bilt.pos.session.settlement.SettlementRecovery>) like a throwing step handler: retry() asks it again, abort() unwinds, abandon() hands the settlement to the register, and any other recovery is refused.

    • onMovement

      public SettlementFlow onMovement(Consumer<SettlementMovement> handler)
      Called after any externally visible money or loyalty movement commits.

      Charge-side movement callbacks are provisional: an abort can unwind them, and retrying, skipping, or replacing a partially committed failed step can reverse that step's movements. Each successful reversal is delivered here as a reversal notice: a movement whose SettlementMovement.isReversal() is true and whose SettlementMovement.getReversedMovement() is the movement reversed, carrying the reversal's own ServiceID and POI reference. Notices never enter the ledger. Earlier successful steps remain committed. Refund allocation movements are not unwound. Use SettlementResult.getMovements() from the successful result as the authoritative final ledger.

    • onSuccess

      public SettlementFlow onSuccess(Consumer<SettlementResult> handler)
      Called after the full sequence completes successfully.

    • onError

      public SettlementFlow onError(Function<SettlementFailure,SettlementRecovery> handler)
      Called when a charge-side step definitively fails, or when automatic TransactionStatus recovery cannot resolve an indeterminate terminal request. A recovered successful request continues without invoking this handler. The returned SettlementRecovery retries recovery, skips the failed step, records an external tender, aborts with unwind, or abandons recovery to the register. For an indeterminate failure delivered here, retry checks TransactionStatus again; skip and external replacement are invalid until the original request is resolved. For refund allocation failures, the handler is a terminal failure notification: the returned recovery decision is ignored, committed refund allocations stay recorded, and the register retries with the same committed allocation prefix. Default charge-side policy: abort().

    • onAbandoned

      public SettlementFlow onAbandoned(Consumer<AbandonedSettlementRecord> handler)

    • onComplete

      public SettlementFlow onComplete(Runnable handler)
      Registers a hook that runs exactly once after settlement completes, on every path — success, failure, unexpected exception, or rejection because the session ended before settlement could run. The place for cleanup that must not leak. A throwing hook is logged, never propagated.

    • execute

      public final void execute()
      Runs the flow asynchronously on the session's operation thread — handlers included, see the class docs — and returns immediately. When the session has already ended and its executor rejects the submission, the flow fails with SessionErrorCode.INVALID_STATE through onError and onComplete.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the flow has already run

    • executeSync

      public final void executeSync()
      Runs the flow blocking — the operation takes its turn on the session's operation thread (queueing behind anything in flight, so a sync call never races an asynchronous one) while the caller waits; handlers dispatch on the calling thread.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the flow has already run

    • get

      public final SettlementResult get()
      Runs the flow if it has not run yet and returns the result. Waits for an in-flight execute() to settle first.
      Throws:
      SessionException - if the flow failed
